screening_decisions.reason: Double-blind randomised trial comparing aminophylline (theophylline analogue) versus placebo in patients with acute ischaemic stroke; treatment administered during the acute hospital period consistent with within 1 week of onset.
Randomised double-blind trial of intravenous aminophylline versus placebo in acute cerebral infarction, with immediate post-injection assessment indicating acute treatment initiation.
Open-label, single-arm dose-escalation safety study (no randomisation or control arm).
Population not limited to acute ischaemic stroke; physiologic metabolism study with mixed interventions and no clear acute stroke RCT against placebo/control.
Randomised cross-over physiological study in patients recovering from stroke; timing from onset is not within the first week and focus is on CBF, not an acute treatment RCT.
Randomised cross-over physiological study in recovering stroke patients; timing likely outside 1 week and not an acute therapeutic RCT.
Physiologic cerebral blood flow study; not a randomised trial in acute ischaemic stroke population versus placebo/control.
Animal (cat) study; not a human randomised trial in acute ischaemic stroke.
Animal (dog) cardiovascular study; not an acute ischaemic stroke RCT versus placebo/control.
Not a randomised controlled trial; appears mechanistic/observational and not confined to acute ischaemic stroke within 1 week.
